questions.question_text: What is the common difference $d$ of the arithmetic progression $13, 8, 3, -2, \dots$?

options.why: Subtracted in the wrong direction ($13 - 8 = 5$) instead of $a_2 - a_1$.
Miscalculated the difference between consecutive terms.
Added an extra unit of difference when subtracting.

questions.question_text: Find the $10$th term of the arithmetic sequence with first term $a = 4$ and common difference $d = 3$.

options.why: Used $a + nd = 4 + 10(3)$ instead of $a + (n - 1)d$.
Multiplied $(n - 2)d = 8(3)$ instead of using $(n - 1) = 9$.
Multiplied the term index by $d$ without adding the first term $a$.

questions.question_text: Which expression gives the $n$th term $a_n$ of the arithmetic sequence $11, 15, 19, 23, \dots$?

options.why: Substituted into $a_n = a + nd$ instead of $a_n = a + (n - 1)d$, giving $11 + 4n$ and leaving the first term as the constant.
Swapped the roles of $a$ and $d$, taking $a = 4$ and $d = 11$, so $4 + (n - 1)(11) = 11n - 7$.
Swapped $a$ and $d$ and also dropped the $(n - 1)$ shift, giving $4 + 11n$.

questions.question_text: How many terms are in the finite arithmetic sequence $5, 13, 21, \dots, 149$?

options.why: Solved $8(n - 1) = 144$ as $n = 18$ forgetting to add $1$.
Divided $149 \div 8$ and rounded without using the first term.
Subtracted $2$ instead of adding $1$ in the rearrangement.

questions.question_text: Find the first negative term of the arithmetic sequence $73, 66, 59, \dots$.

options.why: Evaluated the $13$th term instead of the first negative term ($12$th term).
Found the last positive term rather than the first negative term.
Subtracted the common difference once too many times.

questions.question_text: An arithmetic sequence has $3$rd term $17$ and $7$th term $33$. What is the first term $a$?

options.why: Found the common difference $d = 4$ instead of the first term $a$.
Subtracted $3d$ from $17$ instead of $2d = 8$.
Subtracted only one difference from the third term.

questions.question_text: Which term of the arithmetic sequence $80, 74, 68, \dots$ is equal to $-16$?

options.why: Forgot to add $1$ after dividing $-96$ by $-6$.
Added an extra term when rearranging the linear equation.
Subtracted $1$ instead of adding $1$ to $n - 1 = 16$.

questions.question_text: An arithmetic progression has first term $a = \sqrt{3}$ and common difference $d = 2\sqrt{3}$. Find the exact value of $a_8$.

options.why: Used $a + 8d = \sqrt{3} + 16\sqrt{3}$ instead of $a + 7d$.
Calculated $7 \times 2\sqrt{3}$ but forgot to add the initial term $\sqrt{3}$.
Miscalculated the sum of radical coefficients.
